literal: The prognostication states: "This is called losing its lodge; if not the destruction of an army, there must be the perishing of a state."
idiomatic: The gloss calls it a "lost station" omen: expect either annihilation in the field or outright dynastic collapse.

literal: At this time Yang Hu submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against Wu; the sovereign approved it.
idiomatic: Yang Hu then petitioned for the conquest of Wu, and the throne gave its assent.

literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year the army set out; the Great White first appeared in the west at evening.
idiomatic: That November the host marched; Venus made its first evening appearance in the western sky.

literal: In the third month of the first year of Taikang the Wu army was greatly defeated; Sun Hao bound himself with cord and begged guilt; the state of Wu thereupon perished.
idiomatic: In Taikang 1 (280), third month, Wu’s armies were shattered, Sun Hao surrendered in bonds, and the Wu kingdom ceased to exist.

literal: In the third month of the eighth year of Taikang Spark-Delusion guarded the Heart.
idiomatic: In Taikang 8 (287), third month, Mars stationed in the Heart constellation.

literal: The prognostication states: "The king abominates it."
idiomatic: The canon again warned the sovereign of mortal ill.

literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on yiyou, the emperor died.
idiomatic: On yiyou in the fourth month of Taixi 1 (290) the emperor died.

literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui, Spark-Delusion guarded the Supreme Palace Enclosure for sixty days.
idiomatic: In Emperor Hui’s Yuankang 3 (293), fourth month, Mars lingered inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure for sixty days.

literal: The prognostication states: "The feudal lords and the three dukes plot against their superior; there must be a beheaded minister."
idiomatic: It foretold high nobles scheming against the throne and a minister dying by the axe.

literal: One reading says: "The Son of Heaven loses the state."
idiomatic: Another gloss warned of outright loss of the realm.

literal: That spring the Great White guarded Net, reaching this point for more than a hundred days.
idiomatic: All spring Venus had stationed in the Net asterism—well over a hundred days by then.

literal: The prognostication states: "There is anxiety about urgent edicts."
idiomatic: It portended frantic emergency decrees from the palace.

literal: One reading says: "The minister of state dies."
idiomatic: A variant reading singled out the chief minister’s death.

literal: Also it means the borderlands are not at peace.
idiomatic: The same configuration augured trouble along the frontiers.

literal: Afterward Empress Jia framed and killed the heir apparent.
idiomatic: Soon Empress Jia engineered the crown prince’s murder.

literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, on yiwei, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: On yiwei in the tenth month of Yuankang 6 Venus appeared in broad daylight.

literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Spark-Delusion guarded the Heart.
idiomatic: In the ninth year’s sixth month Mars again stationed in the Heart.

literal: The prognostication states: "The king abominates it."
idiomatic: The sovereign was again marked for calamity.

literal: In the eighth month Spark-Delusion entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Mars moved into the Feathered Forest guard asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "The forbidden troops rise on a great scale."
idiomatic: It foretold palace armies mobilizing en masse.

literal: After this the emperor was seen deposed as supreme emperor; shortly the three princes raised troops to punish Prince Zhao of Zhao, Lun, who thereupon dispatched all the central army troops to oppose them for successive months.
idiomatic: The emperor was soon demoted to retired emperor; then the three princes rose against Prince Sima Lun of Zhao, who threw every central-garrison regiment into months of stalemate.

literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongkang the middle terrace star split, and the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: In Yongkang 1’s third month a Central Court star fractured while Venus shone by day.

literal: The prognostication states: "When terrace stars lose their norm, the three dukes have anxiety."
idiomatic: A fractured terrace star boded ill for the three excellencies.

literal: The Great White seen in daytime means unfilial ministers.
idiomatic: Daylight Venus signals treasonous subjects.

literal: In that month Empress Jia killed the heir apparent; Prince Zhao of Zhao, Lun, soon deposed and killed the empress and beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua.
idiomatic: That same month Empress Jia murdered the crown prince; Sima Lun then toppled and slew the empress and executed Zhang Hua, Minister of Works.
